sections.h2: Where do you record a deed in Baltimore County, Maryland?
sections.html:
Deeds for Baltimore County property are recorded in the Land Records department of the Circuit Court for Baltimore County, inside the Clerk's Office at the County Courts Building, 401 Bosley Avenue, 2nd Floor, Towson, MD 21204. The mailing address is P.O. Box 6754, Towson, MD 21285-6754, and the office is open on weekdays from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

The Maryland Judiciary explains that each county and Baltimore City has its own land records department in the circuit court clerk's office. Baltimore City records its own deeds, so a property inside the independent city is not recorded in Towson. Baltimore County was founded in 1659 and Towson has been its seat since a referendum on February 13, 1854, which is why the court sits there.

sections.h2: What can the Baltimore County land records office record?
sections.html:
The land records office can record any instrument that affects a legal interest in real property, including deeds, mortgages, liens, powers of attorney and certain leases. Clerks accept documents that meet the requirements and reject those that do not, and they cannot help fill out forms or review a document before it is recorded.

That rule is the main reason sellers use a title company or attorney. A rejected deed costs days, and in a sale with a closing date, days matter. Maryland's court system advises consulting a lawyer before recording a new deed.

Useful numbers at the Clerk's Office:

  • Land Records Recording: 410-887-2651
  • Land Records Indexing: 410-887-3088
  • Main number: 410-887-2601; TTY users can dial Maryland Relay at 711
  • Foreclosure department: 410-887-2652

sections.h2: What taxes must be paid before a Baltimore County deed is recorded?
sections.html:
Baltimore County collects its own transfer tax and the state recordation tax before the Clerk's Office will take a deed, and the county's Office of Budget and Finance handles both at a separate counter. Payment goes to the Transfer and Recordation Section at 400 Washington Avenue, Room 154, Towson, MD 21204, and checks are payable to Baltimore County, Maryland.

ItemWhat the county page says
Baltimore County transfer tax1.5% of consideration
State recordation tax$2.50 per $500 (or fraction of $500) of consideration, or of the principal debt secured
Lien certificateRequired for any deed that changes or transfers ownership; the county says a deed without one will not be processed
Maryland State Intake SheetRequired with every deed and property-related document
HoursMonday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

A Maryland legislative services guide also states that the first $22,000 of consideration for a grantee's principal residence is exempt from the Baltimore County transfer tax. Ask the Transfer Tax Section at 410-887-2416 whether your deal qualifies before you count on that credit.

The county's page does not say which party pays. Settle that in the sales contract, and have the title company show each charge on the settlement statement.

sections.h2: Why does a Baltimore County deed need a lien certificate?
sections.html:
The lien certificate lets the county confirm that no taxes or charges are owed on the property account before ownership changes. It costs $55, and the application is available in person or by mail with a self-addressed, stamped envelope.

For a seller, the practical step is to order it as soon as a contract is signed. If tax is owed, the county says in most cases it must be paid before the transfer, which pushes a closing date if you discover a balance the day before settlement. The county's Taxpayer Services line is 410-887-2416 for account-specific questions.

One caution from the county's own page: its lien certificate system was offline during a county update, and no restoration date was listed. Call before you plan a same-day pickup.

sections.h2: Which deeds need approval from the state assessment office?
sections.html:
Agricultural-use deeds and partial-transfer deeds must first be approved by the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation, and Baltimore County lists SDAT's Towson office at 300 East Joppa Road, Room 602.

If you are splitting a lot, build the approval into your timeline. Sending a partial-transfer deed to the Clerk's Office without it risks a rejection, and the county page lists the approval as a requirement for those deed types.

  • Whole-parcel residential deed: intake sheet, lien certificate, tax payment.
  • Agricultural-use deed: the same items plus SDAT approval.
  • Partial-transfer deed: the same items plus SDAT approval.

sections.h2: Can you e-record a deed in Baltimore County?
sections.html:
The Baltimore County Clerk's page says documents cannot be filed directly by electronic transmission under Maryland Rule 1-322, though it links an E-Recording for Land Records page under E-Services. Statewide, the Maryland Judiciary says some counties accept deeds and other documents through Simplifile, and electronic signatures require an Affidavit of Intent to Use Electronic Signature, form CC094.

Because the details differ by county, ask your title company whether it uses an electronic channel in Baltimore County or sends the deed in person. Also remember that the county's tax office sends deed-related messages from a specific email address with the subject line Official Tax Notice, and it asks customers to add that sender to their safe list so the message is not lost in spam.

sections.h2: How do you pay recording fees and get copies in Baltimore County?
sections.html:
The Clerk's Office accepts cash, MasterCard, Visa and Discover, and checks or money orders payable to Clerk of the Circuit Court, but it does not accept personal out-of-state checks or debit cards. The land records fees themselves are in a separate Circuit Court fee schedule, and the amounts were not shown on the pages we reviewed, so check the schedule before you bring payment.

For research, the Maryland State Archives runs a free viewer for deeds at landrec.msa.maryland.gov, and an account is required. Copies from the viewer cost $0.50 per page. Land records documents can also be requested from the Clerk's Office online or by email.

Fees on a Maryland deed are split. The Judiciary says some go to the land records department and some to the local county finance office, which matches what you will see in Towson: one payment at the Clerk's Office and another at the county's Transfer and Recordation Section.

sections.h2: What should an owner do if they inherited a Baltimore County house?
sections.html:
An heir selling a Baltimore County house deals with more than the land records counter. The Clerk's Office lists a Register of Wills at 410-887-6680 and the Orphans' Court at 410-887-6516, and neither can substitute for legal advice from a lawyer.

If taxes were left unpaid, resolve them with the Office of Budget and Finance at 410-887-2404 first, because the lien certificate will show them. The county steps above apply however the house is sold, including an as-is sale.

faqs.q: Where is the Baltimore County Circuit Court land records office?
faqs.a: It is in the Clerk's Office at 401 Bosley Avenue, 2nd Floor, Towson, MD 21204, open weekdays from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Land Records Recording can be reached at 410-887-2651.

faqs.q: What is the Baltimore County transfer tax?
faqs.a: The county page lists a transfer tax of 1.5 percent of consideration. A state legislative guide also says the first $22,000 of consideration for a grantee's principal residence is exempt.

faqs.q: What is the Maryland recordation tax on a Baltimore County deed?
faqs.a: The county page lists a state recordation tax of $2.50 per $500, or fraction of $500, of consideration or of the debt secured. Checks go to Baltimore County, Maryland.

faqs.q: Do I need a lien certificate to record a deed in Baltimore County?
faqs.a: Yes, the county says any deed that changes or transfers ownership needs one, and a deed without it will not be processed. The fee is $55.

faqs.q: Can I record a Baltimore County deed online?
faqs.a: The Clerk's page says documents cannot be filed directly by electronic transmission under Maryland Rule 1-322. It does link an e-recording page, so ask your title company how it submits documents.

faqs.q: Does the Clerk's Office help me fill out a deed?
faqs.a: No, clerks cannot help fill out forms or review documents before recording. Maryland's court system suggests speaking with a lawyer first.
